item.title: AI Governance Committee Charter
item.body_md:
## How to use this charter

Replace every bracketed field. Resist the temptation to widen the membership: a committee that cannot reach a decision is worse than no committee, because it converts refusal into delay and gives everyone something to point at.

This is a template, not legal advice.

---

## 1. Purpose

The [ORGANISATION] AI Governance Committee decides which artificial intelligence systems the organisation may use, on what conditions, and when one must stop. It exists so those decisions are made deliberately by people who can be named, rather than accumulating from individual choices nobody reviewed.

## 2. What it decides

The Committee holds decision rights over:

- Approval of any AI system that touches personal data, customer-facing output, employment decisions, or regulated activity.
- The conditions attached to an approval, including monitoring, review dates and limits of use.
- Suspension or withdrawal of a system already in use.
- The organisation-wide AI policy and any exceptions to it.

The Committee does NOT decide procurement price, vendor selection on commercial terms, or technical implementation. Confusing governance with purchasing is the most common way these bodies become slow and irrelevant.

## 3. Membership

| Seat | Held by | Why the seat exists |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Chair | [ROLE] | Owns the decision and the record of it |
| Risk or compliance | [ROLE] | Regulatory exposure |
| Technology | [ROLE] | What the system actually does |
| Business owner | Rotating, by system | Consequence of a wrong output lands here |
| Data protection | [ROLE] | Lawful basis and personal data |
| Legal | [ROLE] or on call | Contract and liability |

Quorum is [N], and must include the Chair and one of risk or legal. Members may send a delegate with authority to decide; a delegate who must take it back to their own management does not count toward quorum, because that is how a meeting becomes a status update.

## 4. How it meets

- Scheduled every [FREQUENCY]. A standing meeting that is routinely cancelled should be made less frequent rather than left in the calendar as fiction.
- Any member may call an extraordinary meeting for a suspected incident.
- Papers circulate [N] working days ahead. An item without a paper is not decided, it is noted.

## 5. What a submission must contain

A system is not considered without:

1. What it does, in one sentence, in the words of the person accountable for it.
2. Who is affected, including people who are not users.
3. What happens when it is wrong, and how that would be noticed.
4. Data sources, with personal data and third-party data identified.
5. Test results on data the system has not seen, dated.
6. The human override, and who exercises it.
7. Proposed monitoring and review date.

Incomplete submissions are returned rather than approved conditionally. Conditional approval of an unexamined system is the failure mode this Committee exists to prevent.

## 6. Decisions and the record

Each decision is recorded as approved, approved with conditions, deferred with a stated reason, or refused. The record names the decider, not just the Committee. Minutes state what was decided and on what evidence; a minute that records only attendance and outcome is useless to the person who must revisit the decision in two years.

The Committee maintains a register of every AI system in use, its approval status, its conditions, its owner and its next review date. That register is the real product of this Committee. Everything else is process.

## 7. Escalation

The Committee escalates to [BOARD OR EXECUTIVE BODY] where a decision would breach policy, carries risk beyond its delegated authority, or where members cannot agree. Deadlock is escalated rather than resolved by attrition.

## 8. Review of the Committee itself

Annually, the Committee reviews: how many systems it approved, how many it refused, how many were deployed without coming to it at all, and how many approvals were revisited after an incident. The third number is the honest measure of whether this charter describes reality. If nothing has ever been refused and nothing has ever bypassed the Committee, at least one of those figures is wrong.

---

**Adopted:** [DATE]  ·  **Owner:** [ROLE]  ·  **Next review:** [DATE]
